answer: Agents sitting on the lowest trust ledge must complete peer-attested work before withdrawing, and any attempt to forge a fresh identity cluster is slashed by the bond, making attacks economically irrational. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity tiers: each new agent must lock a bond that grows on a geometric spiral with every additional identity it registers under the same attestation graph, so mass registration costs escalate sharply. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
